questions.stem: The diagram shows the sub-atomic particles in an atom of an element.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the name of each of the sub-atomic particles labelled P, Q and R.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Give the name of the part of the atom labelled S.

parts.label: b

questions.stem: A potassium permanganate crystal is placed in a beaker of water. After several days a coloured solution forms.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the names of the two processes that cause the coloured solution to form.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The formula of potassium permanganate is $ \mathrm{KMnO_{4}} $

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: How many different types of atom are in $ \mathrm{KMnO_{4}} $? A 3 B 4 C 6 D 7

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Calculate the relative formula mass $ ( M_{r} ) $ of $ KMnO_{4} $

parts.label: c
parts.text: Potassium permanganate can be used as an oxidising agent. State what is meant by the term oxidising agent.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which of these is the molecular formula of an alkane? A $ C_{2} H_{5} $ B $ C_{4} H_{10} $ C $ C H_{2} C H_{2} $ D $ C H_{3} C H_{2} C H_{3} $

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Which of these has the same empirical formula and molecular formula? A $ \mathrm{C H_{2}} $ B $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{6}} $ C $ \mathrm{C_{3} H_{8}} $ D $ \mathrm{C_{4} H_{10}} $

parts.label: b
parts.text: In the presence of ultraviolet radiation, methane reacts with bromine to form bromomethane and hydrogen bromide.

parts.label: b-i

parts.label: b-ii

parts.text: One mole of an alkane burns completely in oxygen. The equation represents the reaction. $\mathrm {a l k a n e} + x \mathrm {O} _ {2} \rightarrow y \mathrm {C O} _ {2} + z \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$ The numbers x,y and z are used to balance the equation.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: The complete combustion of one mole of the alkane produces 220g of carbon dioxide and 108g of water. Calculate the values of y and z. $[ M _ {\mathrm {r}} \mathrm {o f C O} _ {2} = 4 4 \quad M _ {\mathrm {r}} \mathrm {o f H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} = 1 8 ]$

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Determine the molecular formula of the alkane and the value of x. $x =$

parts.text: When an alkane burns in a limited supply of air, incomplete combustion occurs. Explain why incomplete combustion of an alkane could be harmful to humans.

questions.stem: (a) The diagram represents the structure of copper metal. Explain three properties of copper that make it a suitable metal to use in electrical wiring.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The diagram shows the electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution, using graphite electrodes. Copper forms at the negative electrode and oxygen forms at the positive electrode.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Give the formula of the copper ion and the formula of the sulfate ion in copper(II) sulfate. copper ion sulfate ion

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: State what would be seen at the positive electrode.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Give a test for oxygen.

parts.label: b-iv
parts.text: Give an ionic half-equation for the formation of oxygen at the positive electrode.

parts.label: b-v
parts.text: Suggest why the copper(II) sulfate solution contains some $ \mathrm{O H}^{-} $ ions.

questions.stem: This question is about alcohols, carboxylic acids and esters.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ethanol can be manufactured by the fermentation of a solution of glucose.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Write a word equation for this reaction.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: State the substance that needs to be added for the reaction to occur.

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: State two conditions needed for this reaction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: In the presence of an acid catalyst, ethanoic acid is heated with butanol to form an ester.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Which of these is the formula of the ester? $\mathrm {C H} _ {3} \mathrm {C O O C} _ {3} \mathrm {H} _ {7}$ B $ \mathrm{C H_{3} C O O C_{4} H_{9}} $ C $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{5} C O O C_{4} H_{9}} $ D $ \mathrm{C_{3}H_{7}COOC_{2}H_{5}} $

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: State how you would know that an ester has formed.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Give one use of an ester.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Aspirin is a compound used to reduce pain. Aspirin contains a carboxylic acid functional group and an ester functional group.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: State what is meant by the term functional group.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: This is the structural formula of aspirin. Draw a circle around the carboxylic acid functional group.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Aspirin has this percentage composition by mass. $C = 60.00 \% \quad H = 4.44 \% \quad O = 35.56 \%$ Show by calculation that the empirical formula of aspirin is $ \mathrm{C_{9} H_{8}O_{4}} $

questions.stem: A student uses this method to do a titration. use a measuring cylinder to obtain $ 2 5 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of sodium hydroxide solution transfer the solution to a conical flask add a few drops of universal indicator to the flask fill a burette with dilute sulfuric acid and record the initial burette reading add the acid to the flask, swirling the flask continuously add the acid slowly near the end-point record the final burette reading at the end-point The student repeats the titration until at least two concordant results are obtained.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by concordant results.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain two improvements to the student's method so that more accurate results are obtained.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The student makes the improvements and repeats the titration. The sulfuric acid has a concentration of $ 0. 6 0 0 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3}. $ The sodium hydroxide solution has a concentration of $ 1. 5 0 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3}. $ This is the equation for the reaction. $2 \mathrm {N a O H} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} \rightarrow \mathrm {N a} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} + 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$ Calculate the volume, in $ cm^{3} $ , of sulfuric acid that the student needs to completely react with $ 2 5. 0 \, \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of the sodium hydroxide solution.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The student plans to obtain pure dry crystals of hydrated sodium sulfate. They add the calculated volume of sulfuric acid to $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of the sodium hydroxide solution to form sodium sulfate solution. Describe what the student should do to obtain pure dry crystals of hydrated sodium sulfate from the solution.

questions.stem: In the presence of an iron catalyst, nitrogen reacts with hydrogen to form ammonia. The reaction conditions used are a temperature of $ 4 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ and a pressure of 200 atmospheres. This is the equation for the reaction. $\mathrm {N} _ {2} + 3 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm {N H} _ {3} \quad \Delta H = - 9 2 \mathrm {k J / m o l}$

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what the symbol $ \rightleftharpoons $ represents.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Give the reason for using a catalyst.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The reaction mixture is kept at a pressure of 200 atmospheres, but the temperature is increased to $ 5 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ Explain the effect of this change on the yield of ammonia at equilibrium.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: The reaction mixture is kept at a temperature of $ 4 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ , but the pressure is increased to 300 atmospheres. Explain the effect of this change on the yield of ammonia at equilibrium.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Draw an energy level diagram for the reaction between nitrogen and hydrogen Include the reactants, products and $ \Delta H $ in your diagram.

parts.label: d
parts.text: At the start of the reaction, $ 4 8 \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of nitrogen is added to $ 1 2 0 \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of hydrogen at rtp. $\mathrm {N} _ {2} + 3 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm {N H} _ {3}$ [molar volume of any gas at rtp=24 dm $ ^{3} $]

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Show by calculation that the nitrogen is in excess.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: The yield of ammonia at equilibrium is 20%. Calculate the volume, in $ \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of ammonia formed from $ 1 2 0 \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of hydrogen.
